set.st: Alphonse Bellanguette (Berlanquette), French-Canadian, came 1872 and ran a saloon on the beach 2 mi from Fayette (liquor banned in town); distrusted banks; his wife knew he buried much of his fortune but could not find it. Searches recur. A TreasureNet telling adds the 'Hole in the Ground' saloon of Alph Berlanquette (or Bellanguette) on the beach about 2 miles from Fayette in the 1870s, used by the furnace workers; its owner is the one said to have buried his fortune. In 1930 the Escanaba Daily Press called Berlanquette's hoarded money the Fayette treasure tale 'in which the most credence is placed'. He ran a notorious saloon on the shore of Sand Bay; after his death it became Jim Summers's 'Hole in the Ground', which a mob of about fifty burned. 'Some folks think that Berlanquette's treasure was found': about 1910 a Milwaukee man holding a map from the man who had nursed Berlanquette in his last illness sailed over with an Escanaba friend and, while the friend slept, 'slipped away quietly, dug up the treasure and departed for parts unknown.' (A web article's general 'Fayette treasure' cites no sources; the documented tale is Berlanquette's.) Pin is the Sand Bay settlement at the bay head, not the saloon lot.
set.pl: Sand Bay settlement at the bay head, sec. 8/17 line, about 1.6 mi S of the Fayette townsite (1913 atlas: Fayette P.O.); saloon lot not identified
